title: Security testing: injection, poisoning and tenant isolation
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects security testing: injection, poisoning and tenant isolation with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Gate on zero unauthorized reads/writes and zero canary disclosure.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Prompt injection occurs when untrusted text attempts to redirect model behavior. Indirect injection arrives through retrieved documents, logs or tool results rather than the direct user request. Retrieval poisoning manipulates which evidence is selected; sensitive disclosure exposes data to an unauthorized audience.

These risks are connected but distinct. A document can be relevant yet malicious, or benign yet forbidden to the current tenant. Instructions to ignore prior rules are observable attack content; the enforceable boundary is application policy, not a promise that the model will ignore them.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Build synthetic attacks with a case ID, entry point, requested forbidden effect and expected safe behavior. Include cross-tenant document IDs, fake tool instructions, secrets marked as synthetic canaries and oversized inputs. Assert actual tool effects and returned evidence, not merely whether the answer says it refused.

Authorize before retrieval and tool execution, escape output before display, restrict network destinations and bound model/tool work. Keep adversarial text out of production credentials and services; the lab uses isolated synthetic records.
sections.code:
def allowed(doc,tenant):return doc['tenant']==tenant
assert not allowed({'tenant':'other'},'current')

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A model says it cannot reveal secrets while an earlier tool call already retrieved another tenant's record. A filter removes one injection phrase but an encoded paraphrase bypasses it. The issue is enforcement below the language layer.
Inspect the full trace to identify entry point, trust-boundary crossing and effect. Add a regression case for the invariant, then vary phrasing so the fix is not a single-string deny list.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Gate on zero unauthorized reads/writes and zero canary disclosure. Report false blocks on legitimate queries so security controls do not silently make the assistant unusable.

SDETs should preserve attack provenance, observed effect, defense layer and replay instructions. A passing prompt-level refusal test cannot substitute for permission checks in the service and tool implementations.

    return [c for c in canaries if c in text]
